questions.q: What does a LEFT JOIN from a child table to its parent table, filtered to WHERE <parent key> IS NULL, find?
options: Orphaned rows — child rows whose foreign key value has no matching row in the parent table
Every row that has a NULL value in the child table's primary key
Duplicate rows in the parent table
Rows where the parent and child tables have identical column names
questions.explain: This is the standard T-SQL pattern for finding orphaned rows — child rows pointing at a foreign key value that doesn't exist in the parent table.

questions.q: In a database with a properly enforced foreign key constraint, how many rows should the orphan-finding LEFT JOIN query return?
options: Zero
Exactly one per table
The total row count of the child table
It will always error out
questions.explain: If the foreign key constraint is actually enforced, no child row can reference a nonexistent parent, so the orphan check should return zero rows; finding any usually means the constraint is missing, disabled, or was bypassed.

questions.q: What does pattern profiling with a LIKE expression like '%_@_%._%' check for in an EmailAddress column?
options: Whether each value's shape roughly matches 'something, an @ sign, something, a dot, something' — a fast read, not a full validation rule
Whether the email address belongs to a real, currently active account
The exact number of NULL values in the column
Whether two different tables agree on the same customer's email
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this simple LIKE pattern is a fast, approximate shape check — not a complete email validation rule, which is Lesson 14's territory.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say relationship and pattern profiling catch problems that column profiling (Lesson 8) alone misses?
options: Because a column can look perfectly healthy in isolation while the relationship it depends on is broken, or while its values don't match an expected shape
Because column profiling cannot run any SQL queries at all
Because relationship profiling never requires writing any SQL
Because pattern profiling only works on numeric columns
questions.explain: Column-level checks (NULL rate, min/max, frequency) don't reveal broken cross-table relationships or value-shape mismatches — that's what relationship and pattern profiling are for.
